subject: BridgeView trial: technical acceptance & streaming integration playbook
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.inference.com>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@bridgeview.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.inference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference.com>
Date: 2027-04-25T15:10:00-07:00
Subject: BridgeView trial: technical acceptance & streaming integration playbook

Hi Liam — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed POC plan so we have the same frame for kickoff: 

Call recap
- Primary goal: validate low-latency chat + retrieval workflow for customer support (routing, real-time snippets, and KB-augmented replies).
- Success criteria you called out: p95 latency < 150ms (generation time), sustained throughput ~50 req/s during peak test window, and no meaningful regressions vs your in-house baseline on intent classification (F1 within 2 points).

Proposed evaluation plan (POC / 3-week trial)
1) Week 0 (prep): data schema & sample payloads, access to staging SSO, shared signing of GDPR addendum.
2) Week 1 (integration): SDK integration + streaming route, implement retrieval plugin (tool calling), initial smoke tests.
3) Week 2 (load & quality): run synthetic traffic ramp, collect latency/throughput, run labeled prompt set for quality regression checks.
4) Week 3 (acceptance): joint review against success criteria, live validation with a fenced user group.

Integration specifics (technical highlights)
- SDK: Redwood JS/Python SDK (we'll share a pre-release branch) — primary routes: POST /v1/generate for sync, POST /v1/streams for streaming (SSE).
- Streaming: recommend SSE for your browser agents (fallback to websockets for mobile) — supports incremental delta tokens + per-token metadata.
- Tool calling: function/tool registry approach — retrieval plugin will call your internal KB via an authenticated service account; we support deterministic tool responses and tool result caching.
- KV cache: we can surface session-level KV cache pinned to a session_id to avoid re-fetches for repeated context.

Ownership (proposed)
- Redwood: Naomi (AM) owner for onboarding, Marcus (runtime lead) for performance tuning, Marissa (CS) for acceptance runbooks.
- BridgeView: Liam (eng lead) owner, TBD (infra) for staging creds, procurement for contract/SLA.

Next steps / asks from BridgeView
- Confirm sample payloads and a small dataset (10–50 examples) by 2027-05-01.
- Confirm kickoff date (we propose 2027-05-03; if not, suggest an alternate).
- Share staging AWS role or service account for retrieval plugin (least privilege).

Attachments: I attached the "redwood-sdk-integration-checklist.xlsx" with the minimal endpoints and example payloads. Also linking an editable playbook in Drive.

Thanks — happy to walk through the plan in 20 minutes if you want to lock the kickoff.

—Naomi
Naomi Feldman
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
naomi.feldman@redwood.inference.com
+1 (415) 555-0122

From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@bridgeview.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.inference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference.com>
Date: 2027-04-26T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: BridgeView trial: technical acceptance & streaming integration playbook

Thanks Naomi — this is helpful and captures the scope. A couple quick clarifications from our side: 

1) Payloads & sizes: our typical user event payloads average ~1.8KB after JSON and context; the long-tail has some chats up to ~16KB (attachments stripped). Will that affect the streaming path?
2) Embeddings & cache: we plan to send pre-computed embeddings for user history; can Redwood accept embeddings inline and skip internal recompute? Also, confirm how session KV cache TTLs are surfaced so we can tune.
3) Tool calling: our retrieval service requires signed JWT from a service account. Can you support short-lived signed tokens (1–5m) for plugin calls?

Timeline: May 3 is tight for our infra lead. Can we move kickoff to May 5? That gives us two extra days to prepare credentials.

I'm attaching the BridgeView staging data schema (bridgeview-data-schema.pdf) for your review — it shows the event formats and the retrieval API surface.

If you can confirm support for: (a) inline embeddings, (b) signed short-lived tokens for retrieval, and (c) SSE handling of payloads up to 20KB (with chunking), we'll be ready to confirm May 5.

—Liam
Liam O'Connor
Head of Engineering, BridgeView AI
liam.oconnor@bridgeview.ai

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.inference.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.inference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference.com>
Date: 2027-04-26T10:30:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: Re: BridgeView trial: technical acceptance & streaming integration playbook

Internal notes / action items — do not forward to customer as-is.

- Streaming support: we can handle 20KB payloads on SSE with chunking; will need to enable chunked_payloads flag on the trial tenant. Marcus to flip in staging (ETA 48h).
- Inline embeddings: supported via the embeddings field; mark "embeddings_mode": "external" in the workflow. We'll skip internal embedding compute if embeddings present and valid shape.
- Signed tokens: runtime supports short-lived signed JWTs for plugin calls — will provide example middleware and a small helper library (node/python) to mint tokens via our KMS-backed signing service.
- Capacity: reserve a 2-GPU dev queue for the first 2 weeks (we'll throttle to emulate peak). Ops: please confirm by EOD.

Owners (finalized)
- Runtime & infra: Marcus Lin (marcus.lin@redwood.inference.com) — streaming + token support + capacity
- Customer success & acceptance: Marissa Cole (marissa.cole@redwood.inference.com) — test harness, prompt set, and quality regression checks
- AM & coordination: Naomi Feldman — kickoff, SOW, scheduling

I'll prepare a short internal runbook with the checklist and sample payloads. Link to internal runbook draft: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1internal_runbook_bridgeview (internal access only).

Marcus
Marcus Lin
Principal Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.inference.com>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@bridgeview.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.inference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference.com>
Date: 2027-04-27T08:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: BridgeView trial: technical acceptance & streaming integration playbook

Perfect — thanks Liam. Confirming the items below so we can lock kickoff for 2027-05-05 at 09:00 PT (virtual):

Confirmed support
- Inline embeddings: YES — include embeddings in the "embeddings" field of the request and set embeddings_mode to "external". Runtime will skip recompute and populate cost metrics accordingly.
- Short-lived signed tokens for retrieval: YES — we'll provide a small helper (node/python) to mint 2–5m JWTs. Marcus will share the repo during week 0.
- SSE payloads up to 20KB: YES (chunked_payloads enabled). We recommend trimming unnecessary fields from the payload to reduce latency.

Deliverables before kickoff (please):
- BridgeView: staging service account + IAM role by 2027-05-03 EOD.
- BridgeView: sample payloads (10–50 examples) and label set for acceptance tests by 2027-05-03 EOD.
- Redwood: finalized integration checklist (attached) + pre-release SDK branch + internal runbook link.

Links & attachments
- Integration checklist (attached): redwood-sdk-integration-checklist.xlsx
- Playbook (editable): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c_bridgeview_trial_playbook
- SOW (DocuSign): https://www.docusign.net/embeddedSigning?token=ABCD1234-bridgeview-sow

I'll schedule the kickoff invite once you confirm May 5 works for your infra lead. Also looping Marcus and Marissa for any final tech constraints.

Thanks — excited to get this running.

—Naomi
